## Overview

This page compares LLM‑generated ratings with human evaluations across the Unjournal criteria. We (i) harmonize the two sources to a common set of metrics and paper IDs, (ii) compute paired scores per *(paper, metric)*, and (iii) summarize agreement using distributional views and reliability statistics.  
The scatter plot in @fig-scatter-selector and overlaid histograms in @fig-hist-static show how the two raters spread scores within each metric.


## Data & Harmonization

- Sources. LLM ratings come from `results/metrics_long.csv` (rendered in the previous chapter). Human ratings are imported from your hand‑coded spreadsheet and mapped to LLM paper IDs via `UJ_map.csv`.  
- Metric alignment. Human criteria are recoded to the LLM schema (e.g., `claims` → `claims_evidence`, `adv_knowledge` → `advancing_knowledge`, etc.). If humans provided both `gp_relevance` and `real_world`, we fold these into the single LLM metric `global_relevance`.  
- Pairing. For each *(paper, metric)*, multiple human entries (if any) are averaged to one human midpoint. We then pair that with the corresponding LLM midpoint, yielding one (LLM, Human) pair per *(paper, metric)* used throughout the analyses.  
- Uncertainty fields. Where available, we carry lower/upper bounds for both LLM and humans; these are used in optional uncertainty checks but do not affect the mid‑point comparisons below.

```{python}
#| label: load-and-merge
#| echo: false

# Files
LLM_FILE   = "results/metrics_long.csv"
HUMAN_FILE = "UJ_ratings/rsx_evalr_rating (7).csv"
IMAP_FILE  = "UJ_ratings/UJ_map.csv"

llm   = pd.read_csv(LLM_FILE)
human = pd.read_csv(HUMAN_FILE)
imap  = pd.read_csv(IMAP_FILE)

# 1) Map human 'criteria' → LLM metric names
crit_map = {
    "overall":          "overall",
    "claims":           "claims_evidence",
    "methods":          "methods",
    "adv_knowledge":    "advancing_knowledge",
    "logic_comms":      "logic_communication",
    "open_sci":         "open_science",
    "gp_relevance":     "global_relevance",
    "real_world":       "global_relevance",  # fold-in
    "merits_journal":   None,
    "journal_predict":  None
}
human["metric"] = human["criteria"].map(crit_map)
human = human[human["metric"].notna()].copy()

# 2) Normalize titles to join robustly
def _norm_title(s: str) -> str:
    s = str(s)
    s = s.replace("’", "'").replace("–","-").replace("—","-")
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()
    return s

human["research_norm"] = human["research"].map(_norm_title).str.lower()
imap["research_norm"]  = imap["research"].map(_norm_title).str.lower()

# 3) Attach LLM paper id to human rows
human = human.merge(imap[["paper","research_norm"]], on="research_norm", how="left")

# 4) Diagnostics
missing_id  = sorted(human[human.paper.isna()]["research"].unique())
missing_llm = sorted(set(llm.paper.unique()) - set(human.paper.dropna().unique()))
if missing_id:
    print("⚠️ Human titles without LLM id (fill 'paper' in UJ_map.csv):")
    for t in missing_id: print("   •", t)
if missing_llm:
    print("\n⚠️ LLM papers with no human match:")
    for p in missing_llm: print("   •", p)

# 5) Collapse human repeats to means (per paper×metric)
human_use = (human
    .dropna(subset=["paper","metric","middle_rating"])
    .groupby(["paper","metric"], as_index=False)
    .agg(midpoint_human=("middle_rating","mean"),
         lower_human   =("lower_CI","mean"),
         upper_human   =("upper_CI","mean"),
         n_human       =("middle_rating","size"))
)

# 6) Select/rename LLM columns
llm_use = (llm[["paper","metric","midpoint","lower_bound","upper_bound"]]
           .rename(columns={"midpoint":"midpoint_llm",
                            "lower_bound":"lower_llm",
                            "upper_bound":"upper_llm"}))

# 7) Merge pairs
merged = llm_use.merge(human_use, on=["paper","metric"], how="inner")

print(f"✅ merged rows: {len(merged)}  "
      f"({merged.paper.nunique()} papers × {merged.metric.nunique()} metrics)")

# Long form for distribution plots
ratings_long = pd.concat([
    merged[["paper","metric","midpoint_llm"]]
        .rename(columns={"midpoint_llm":"score"}).assign(rater="LLM"),
    merged[["paper","metric","midpoint_human"]]
        .rename(columns={"midpoint_human":"score"}).assign(rater="Human")
], ignore_index=True)
```

```{python}
# Keep per‑rater rows (after mapping; before averaging)
human_raw = human.dropna(subset=["paper","metric","middle_rating"]).copy()

# Try to detect a rater id column; otherwise make one per (paper, metric)
cands = [c for c in human_raw.columns if c.lower() in
         ["rater","reviewer","evaluator","coder","annotator","user","name",
          "id","uid","user_id","evaluator_id","reviewer_id"]]
if cands:

    human_raw["rater_id"] = human_raw[rid_col].astype(str)
else:
    human_raw["rater_id"] = (human_raw
                             .groupby(["paper","metric"])
                             .cumcount()
                             .add(1)
                             .map(lambda i: f"R{i}"))

# One row per paper×metric with LLM midpoint (for joining)
llm_single = llm_use[["paper","metric","midpoint_llm"]].drop_duplicates()
```

```{python}
#| label: agreement-helpers
#| echo: false

def pair_llm_human(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return (paper, metric, LLM, Human) single-row pairs."""
    return (df[["paper","metric","midpoint_llm","midpoint_human"]]
            .dropna()
            .rename(columns={"midpoint_llm":"LLM","midpoint_human":"Human"}))

def bin_together(a, b, n_bins=5, strategy="quantile"):
    """
    Bin two continuous arrays with shared edges (for κ).
    - 'quantile' bins are robust to skew.
    - fallback to equal-width if quantiles collapse.
    """
    both = pd.Series(np.r_[a, b]).dropna()
    if both.nunique() <= max(3, n_bins):
        # Already discrete-ish: map unique sorted values to 0..K-1
        uniq = np.sort(both.unique())
        mapping = {v:i for i,v in enumerate(uniq)}
        return np.vectorize(mapping.get)(a), np.vectorize(mapping.get)(b), len(uniq)
    if strategy == "quantile":
        qs = both.quantile(np.linspace(0, 1, n_bins+1)).values
        edges = np.unique(qs)
        if len(edges) - 1 < 2:
            strategy = "equal"
    if strategy == "equal":
        lo, hi = float(both.min()), float(both.max())
        edges = np.linspace(lo, hi, n_bins+1)
    edges[0] -= 1e-9; edges[-1] += 1e-9
    a_bin = pd.cut(a, bins=edges, labels=False, include_lowest=True)
    b_bin = pd.cut(b, bins=edges, labels=False, include_lowest=True)
    k = int(np.nanmax([a_bin.max(), b_bin.max()]) + 1)
    return np.asarray(a_bin), np.asarray(b_bin), k

def weighted_kappa(a, b, k=None, weights="quadratic"):
    """
    Cohen's weighted kappa for ordinal labels 0..k-1.
    weights: 'quadratic' (default), 'linear', or None (unweighted).
    """
    a = np.asarray(a, dtype=int)
    b = np.asarray(b, dtype=int)
    if k is None:
        k = int(max(a.max(), b.max()) + 1)
    if k <= 1:  # not enough categories
        return np.nan

    # Observed agreement matrix (proportions)
    M = np.zeros((k, k), dtype=float)
    for i, j in zip(a, b):
        if np.isfinite(i) and np.isfinite(j):
            M[i, j] += 1
    if M.sum() == 0:
        return np.nan
    M = M / M.sum()

    # Expected by marginals
    r = M.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    c = M.sum(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    E = r @ c

    # Weight matrix
    I = np.arange(k)[:, None]
    J = np.arange(k)[None, :]
    if weights == "quadratic":
        W = ((I - J)**2) / ((k - 1)**2 if k > 1 else 1)
    elif weights == "linear":
        W = np.abs(I - J) / (k - 1 if k > 1 else 1)
    else:
        W = (I != J).astype(float)


    num = (W * M).sum()
    den = (W * E).sum()
    return np.nan if den == 0 else 1.0 - num / den

def agreement_summary(merged_df, n_bins=5, bin_strategy="quantile"):
    """
    Per-metric agreement: Pearson, Spearman, mean/median bias, κ (unweighted & quadratic).
    """
    pair = pair_llm_human(merged_df)
    rows = []
    for metric, g in pair.groupby("metric"):
        llm = g["LLM"].to_numpy()
        hum = g["Human"].to_numpy()

        pr, pr_p = (np.nan, np.nan)
        sr, sr_p = (np.nan, np.nan)
        if len(g) >= 2:
            try: pr, pr_p = pearsonr(llm, hum)
            except Exception: pass
            try: sr, sr_p = spearmanr(llm, hum)
            except Exception: pass

        diff = llm - hum
        mb, medb = float(np.mean(diff)), float(np.median(diff))

        a_bin, b_bin, k = bin_together(llm, hum, n_bins=n_bins, strategy=bin_strategy)
        k_unw = weighted_kappa(a_bin, b_bin, k=k, weights=None)
        k_quad = weighted_kappa(a_bin, b_bin, k=k, weights="quadratic")

        rows.append(dict(
            metric=metric, n=len(g),
            pearson=pr, spearman=sr,
            mean_bias=mb, median_bias=medb,
            kappa_unw=k_unw, kappa_quad=k_quad
        ))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("metric").reset_index(drop=True)
    return out

def overall_stats(merged_df, n_bins=5, bin_strategy="quantile"):
    """
    Overall (across all metrics) Pearson and κ (unweighted & quadratic),
    plus overall MAD.
    """
    pair = pair_llm_human(merged_df)
    llm = pair["LLM"].to_numpy()
    hum = pair["Human"].to_numpy()
    pr = pearsonr(llm, hum)[0] if len(pair) >= 2 else np.nan
    mad = float(np.mean(np.abs(llm - hum))) if len(pair) else np.nan
    a_bin, b_bin, k = bin_together(llm, hum, n_bins=n_bins, strategy=bin_strategy)
    k_unw = weighted_kappa(a_bin, b_bin, k=k, weights=None)
    k_quad = weighted_kappa(a_bin, b_bin, k=k, weights="quadratic")
    return dict(pearson=pr, mad=mad, kappa_unw=k_unw, kappa_quad=k_quad, n=len(pair))

```


















## Distribution of ratings



```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter-selector
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Interactive scatter: choose a metric to see LLM vs Human. Dashed line = perfect agreement; annotation shows Pearson r and Spearman ρ."

import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Build the paired data (paper, metric, LLM, Human)
pair_all = pair_llm_human(merged)

# If some metrics have <2 points, we keep them but annotate with NaN
cats = sorted(pair_all["metric"].unique())

# Global square axis range so the 45° line is visually meaningful
x_min = float(pair_all["Human"].min())
x_max = float(pair_all["Human"].max())
y_min = float(pair_all["LLM"].min())
y_max = float(pair_all["LLM"].max())
lo = min(x_min, y_min)
hi = max(x_max, y_max)
pad = 0.05 * (hi - lo if hi > lo else 1.0)
x0, x1 = lo - pad, hi + pad
y0, y1 = lo - pad, hi + pad

fig = go.Figure()
annots = []

for i, cat in enumerate(cats):
    g = pair_all.loc[pair_all["metric"] == cat].copy()
    # Correlations per metric (handle small n)
    if len(g) >= 2:
        r_p = pearsonr(g["Human"], g["LLM"])[0]
        r_s = spearmanr(g["Human"], g["LLM"])[0]
    else:
        r_p = np.nan
        r_s = np.nan

    # Points
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=g["Human"], y=g["LLM"],
        mode="markers",
        name=cat,
        text=g["paper"],
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Human=%{x:.1f}<br>LLM=%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        marker=dict(size=8, color=UJ_ORANGE, line=dict(color="rgba(50,50,50,0.5)", width=0.5)),
        visible=(i == 0)
    ))

    # Per-metric annotation (updated by the dropdown)
    annots.append(dict(
        x=x0 + 0.05*(x1 - x0),
        y=y1 - 0.05*(y1 - y0),
        xref="x", yref="y",
        showarrow=False,
        text=f"Pearson r = {r_p:.2f}; Spearman ρ = {r_s:.2f}",
        font=dict(size=12, color="#222")
    ))

# 45° agreement line
fig.add_shape(
    type="line", x0=x0, y0=x0, x1=x1, y1=y1,
    line=dict(color="rgba(120,120,120,0.5)", dash="dot")
)

# Dropdown buttons: toggle which metric's points are visible and swap annotation
buttons = []
for i, cat in enumerate(cats):
    vis = [False]*len(cats)
    vis[i] = True
    buttons.append(dict(
        method="update",
        label=cat.replace("_"," ").title(),
        args=[
            {"visible": vis},
            {
              "title": f"LLM vs Human by paper — {cat.replace('_',' ').title()}",
              "annotations": [annots[i]]
            }
        ]
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    title=f"LLM vs Human by paper — {cats[0].replace('_',' ').title()}",
    xaxis_title="Human score",
    yaxis_title="LLM score",
    xaxis=dict(range=[x0, x1]),
    yaxis=dict(range=[y0, y1], scaleanchor="x", scaleratio=1),  # keep 45° line at 45°
    updatemenus=[dict(
        type="dropdown",
        x=1, xanchor="right",
        y=1.15, yanchor="top",
        showactive=True,
        buttons=buttons
    )]
)
fig

```



```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter-humans-range
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "LLM vs Human by paper (all human raters shown). For each paper: green dots are individual human ratings; orange diamond is LLM vs human mean with horizontal whiskers spanning the full human range."

import plotly.graph_objects as go

metrics = sorted(human_raw["metric"].unique())

# Precompute per‑metric summaries: human mean/min/max merged with LLM
summ_by_metric = {}
indiv_by_metric = {}

for m in metrics:
    # per-paper human summary
    hsum = (human_raw.loc[human_raw["metric"] == m]
            .groupby("paper", as_index=False)
            .agg(mean_human=("middle_rating","mean"),
                 min_human =("middle_rating","min"),
                 max_human =("middle_rating","max"),
                 n_human   =("middle_rating","size")))
    # join LLM
    joined = (hsum.merge(llm_single[llm_single["metric"] == m][["paper","midpoint_llm"]],
                         on="paper", how="inner"))
    summ_by_metric[m] = joined

    # individual human points with LLM on y
    indiv = (human_raw.loc[human_raw["metric"] == m, ["paper","rater_id","middle_rating","metric"]]
             .merge(llm_single[llm_single["metric"] == m][["paper","midpoint_llm"]],
                    on="paper", how="inner"))
    indiv_by_metric[m] = indiv

# Global axis limits (pooled across metrics)
all_h_means = np.concatenate([df["mean_human"].to_numpy() for df in summ_by_metric.values() if len(df)])
all_h_mins  = np.concatenate([df["min_human"].to_numpy()  for df in summ_by_metric.values() if len(df)])
all_h_maxs  = np.concatenate([df["max_human"].to_numpy()  for df in summ_by_metric.values() if len(df)])
all_llm     = np.concatenate([df["midpoint_llm"].to_numpy() for df in summ_by_metric.values() if len(df)])

if all_h_means.size:
    x_lo = float(np.nanmin(np.concatenate([all_h_mins, all_h_means, all_h_maxs])))
    x_hi = float(np.nanmax(np.concatenate([all_h_mins, all_h_means, all_h_maxs])))
    y_lo = float(np.nanmin(all_llm))
    y_hi = float(np.nanmax(all_llm))
else:
    x_lo = y_lo = 0.0
    x_hi = y_hi = 100.0

pad_x = 0.05*(x_hi - x_lo if x_hi > x_lo else 1.0)
pad_y = 0.05*(y_hi - y_lo if y_hi > y_lo else 1.0)
x0, x1 = x_lo - pad_x, x_hi + pad_x
y0, y1 = y_lo - pad_y, y_hi + pad_y

fig = go.Figure()
annots = []
traces_per_metric = 2  # (1) individual human dots, (2) LLM vs human mean + range

for i, m in enumerate(metrics):
    J = summ_by_metric[m]
    I = indiv_by_metric[m]

    # Correlations for the selected metric (LLM vs human mean)
    if len(J) >= 2:
        r_p = pearsonr(J["mean_human"], J["midpoint_llm"])[0]
        r_s = spearmanr(J["mean_human"], J["midpoint_llm"])[0]
    else:
        r_p = np.nan
        r_s = np.nan

    # (1) Individual human dots (many)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=I["middle_rating"], y=I["midpoint_llm"],
        mode="markers",
        name="Human raters",
        marker=dict(size=6, color=UJ_GREEN, opacity=0.55,
                    line=dict(width=0.5, color="rgba(50,50,50,0.35)")),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Human=%{x:.1f}<br>LLM=%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        text=[f"{p} — {r}" for p, r in zip(I["paper"], I["rater_id"])],
        visible=(i == 0)
    ))

    # Compute asymmetric error bars (min/max around mean)
    err_plus  = (J["max_human"]  - J["mean_human"]).to_numpy()
    err_minus = (J["mean_human"] - J["min_human"]).to_numpy()

    # (2) LLM vs human mean (orange diamond) with human range whiskers (green)
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=J["mean_human"], y=J["midpoint_llm"],
        mode="markers",
        name="LLM vs human mean",
        marker=dict(size=9, color=UJ_ORANGE, symbol="diamond",
                    line=dict(width=0.6, color="rgba(50,50,50,0.4)")),
        error_x=dict(type="data", symmetric=False, array=err_plus, arrayminus=err_minus,
                     color=UJ_GREEN, thickness=1.25, width=0),
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Human mean=%{x:.1f}<br>LLM=%{y:.1f}<br>Human range=[%{customdata[0]:.1f}, %{customdata[1]:.1f}]<extra></extra>",
        text=J["paper"],
        customdata=np.stack([J["min_human"], J["max_human"]], axis=1),
        visible=(i == 0)
    ))

    # Per‑metric annotation (updated by the dropdown)
    annots.append(dict(
        x=x0 + 0.05*(x1 - x0),
        y=y1 - 0.05*(y1 - y0),
        xref="x", yref="y",
        showarrow=False,
        text=f"{m.replace('_',' ').title()} — Pearson r = {r_p:.2f}; Spearman ρ = {r_s:.2f}",
        font=dict(size=12, color="#222")
    ))

# 45° equality line
fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=x0, y0=x0, x1=x1, y1=y1,
              line=dict(color="rgba(120,120,120,0.5)", dash="dot"))

# Dropdown logic: two traces per metric (human dots, mean+range)
buttons = []
for i, m in enumerate(metrics):
    vis = [False] * (len(metrics) * traces_per_metric)
    vis[2*i + 0] = True  # human dots
    vis[2*i + 1] = True  # mean+range
    buttons.append(dict(
        method="update",
        label=m.replace("_"," ").title(),
        args=[
            {"visible": vis},
            {"title": f"LLM vs Human — all raters shown — {m.replace('_',' ').title()}",
             "annotations": [annots[i]]}
        ]
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    title=f"LLM vs Human — all raters shown — {metrics[0].replace('_',' ').title()}",
    xaxis_title="Human score (x) — dots = individual raters; whiskers = full human range",
    yaxis_title="LLM score (y)",
    xaxis=dict(range=[x0, x1]),
    yaxis=dict(range=[y0, y1], scaleanchor="x", scaleratio=1),
    updatemenus=[dict(type="dropdown", x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.15, yanchor="top",
                      showactive=True, buttons=buttons)]
)
fig
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-scatter-ellipses
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "LLM vs Human with CI ellipses. Each ellipse spans human (x) and LLM (y) CIs; center is at midpoints. Use the dropdown to change metric."

import plotly.graph_objects as go

def _ellipse_xy(cx, cy, rx, ry, n=64):
    t = np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, n)
    return cx + rx*np.cos(t), cy + ry*np.sin(t)

metrics = sorted(merged["metric"].unique())

# Per-metric subset with needed CI columns; drop rows missing any CI
metric_rows = {
    m: merged.loc[
        (merged["metric"]==m) &
        merged[["midpoint_human","midpoint_llm","lower_human","upper_human","lower_llm","upper_llm"]].notna().all(axis=1),
        ["paper","midpoint_human","midpoint_llm","lower_human","upper_human","lower_llm","upper_llm"]
    ].copy()
    for m in metrics
}

# Correlations per metric (midpoints)
r_stats = {}
for m, J in metric_rows.items():
    if len(J) >= 2:
        r_p = pearsonr(J["midpoint_human"], J["midpoint_llm"])[0]
        r_s = spearmanr(J["midpoint_human"], J["midpoint_llm"])[0]
    else:
        r_p = np.nan; r_s = np.nan
    r_stats[m] = (r_p, r_s)

# Global square axis range across all metrics (robust to outliers)
all_x = np.concatenate([j["midpoint_human"].to_numpy() for j in metric_rows.values() if len(j)])
all_y = np.concatenate([j["midpoint_llm"].to_numpy()   for j in metric_rows.values() if len(j)])
if all_x.size and all_y.size:
    lo = float(min(all_x.min(), all_y.min()))
    hi = float(max(all_x.max(), all_y.max()))
else:
    lo, hi = 0.0, 100.0
pad = 0.05 * (hi - lo if hi > lo else 1.0)
x0, x1 = lo - pad, hi + pad
y0, y1 = lo - pad, hi + pad

fig = go.Figure()
annots = []
trace_offsets = []  # starting index for each metric, to build the visibility mask

for m in metrics:
    start_idx = len(fig.data)
    J = metric_rows[m].copy()
    if J.empty:
        # add a tiny placeholder so dropdown works
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(x=[], y=[], mode="markers", showlegend=False))
        annots.append(dict(
            x=x0 + 0.05*(x1-x0), y=y1 - 0.05*(y1-y0),
            xref="x", yref="y", showarrow=False,
            text=f"{m.replace('_',' ').title()} — no rows with both CIs available",
            font=dict(size=12, color="#444")))
        trace_offsets.append((start_idx, len(fig.data)-1))
        continue

    # Radii from CIs (half widths); clamp tiny/negative to 0
    rx = 0.5*(J["upper_human"] - J["lower_human"]).clip(lower=0).to_numpy()
    ry = 0.5*(J["upper_llm"]   - J["lower_llm"]).clip(lower=0).to_numpy()
    cx = J["midpoint_human"].to_numpy()
    cy = J["midpoint_llm"].to_numpy()

    # (A) Ellipses per paper (semi‑transparent, no legend spam; legend stub added later)
    for paper, xi, yi, rxi, ryi in zip(J["paper"], cx, cy, rx, ry):
        if not (np.isfinite(xi) and np.isfinite(yi) and np.isfinite(rxi) and np.isfinite(ryi)):
            continue
        ex, ey = _ellipse_xy(xi, yi, rxi, ryi, n=60)
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=ex, y=ey, mode="lines",
            line=dict(color="rgba(0,158,115,0.55)", width=1),  # green outline
            fill="toself", fillcolor="rgba(230,159,0,0.10)",   # orange wash
            hovertemplate=(
                f"<b>{paper}</b><br>"
                "Human mid=%{customdata[0]:.1f}  (±%{customdata[2]:.1f})<br>"
                "LLM   mid=%{customdata[1]:.1f}  (±%{customdata[3]:.1f})<extra></extra>"
            ),
            customdata=np.column_stack([np.repeat(xi, len(ex)),
                                        np.repeat(yi, len(ex)),
                                        np.repeat(rxi, len(ex)),
                                        np.repeat(ryi, len(ex))]),
            showlegend=False,
            visible=False  # will be turned on by dropdown
        ))
    # (optional) Individual human dots on top of ellipses
    I = human_raw.loc[human_raw["metric"]==m, ["paper","rater_id","middle_rating"]]
    I = I.merge(J[["paper","midpoint_llm"]], on="paper", how="inner")
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=I["middle_rating"], y=I["midpoint_llm"],
        mode="markers", name="Human raters",
        marker=dict(size=5, color=UJ_GREEN, opacity=0.45, line=dict(width=0.5, color="rgba(50,50,50,0.25)")),
        text=[f"{p} — {r}" for p, r in zip(I["paper"], I["rater_id"])],
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Human=%{x:.1f}<br>LLM=%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        showlegend=True, visible=False
    ))

    # (B) Centers (orange diamonds) — single trace per metric
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=J["midpoint_human"], y=J["midpoint_llm"],
        mode="markers", name="Midpoints",
        marker=dict(size=9, color=UJ_ORANGE, symbol="diamond",
                    line=dict(color="rgba(50,50,50,0.35)", width=0.6)),
        text=J["paper"],
        hovertemplate="<b>%{text}</b><br>Human mid=%{x:.1f}<br>LLM mid=%{y:.1f}<extra></extra>",
        showlegend=True,
        visible=False
    ))

    # (C) One dummy, invisible point to show a single legend item for the ellipses
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[None], y=[None], mode="lines", name="CI ellipse (human × LLM)",
        line=dict(color="rgba(0,158,115,0.70)"), fill="toself",
        showlegend=True, visible=False
    ))

    r_p, r_s = r_stats[m]
    annots.append(dict(
        x=x0 + 0.05*(x1-x0), y=y1 - 0.05*(y1-y0),
        xref="x", yref="y", showarrow=False,
        text=f"{m.replace('_',' ').title()} — Pearson r = {r_p:.2f}; Spearman ρ = {r_s:.2f}",
        font=dict(size=12, color="#222")
    ))

    trace_offsets.append((start_idx, len(fig.data)-1))

# 45° equality line
fig.add_shape(type="line", x0=x0, y0=x0, x1=x1, y1=y1,
              line=dict(color="rgba(120,120,120,0.5)", dash="dot"))

# Dropdown buttons: toggle traces belonging to the selected metric
buttons = []
total_traces = len(fig.data)
for i, m in enumerate(metrics):
    vis = [False]*total_traces
    s, e = trace_offsets[i]
    for k in range(s, e+1):
        vis[k] = True
    buttons.append(dict(
        method="update",
        label=m.replace("_"," ").title(),
        args=[{"visible": vis},
              {"title": f"LLM vs Human — CI ellipses — {m.replace('_',' ').title()}",
               "annotations": [annots[i]]}]
    ))

# Initialize first metric visible
init_vis = [False]*len(fig.data)
s0, e0 = trace_offsets[0]
for k in range(s0, e0+1):
    init_vis[k] = True

fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    title=f"LLM vs Human — CI ellipses — {metrics[0].replace('_',' ').title()}",
    xaxis_title="Human midpoint (x)",
    yaxis_title="LLM midpoint (y)",
    xaxis=dict(range=[x0, x1]),
    yaxis=dict(range=[y0, y1], scaleanchor="x", scaleratio=1),
    updatemenus=[dict(type="dropdown", x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.15, yanchor="top",
                      showactive=True, buttons=buttons)]
)
fig.update_traces(visible=False)
for k, v in enumerate(init_vis):
    fig.data[k].visible = v

fig
```

## Differences by paper and metric

For each *(paper, metric)*, we plot LLM − Human difference in @fig-heatmap-static. Green means the LLM is lower than the human midpoint; orange means higher.  

  - Vertical stripes (by metric) suggest a metric‑specific bias (LLM systematically up/down on that metric).  
  - Horizontal stripes (by paper) flag paper‑specific disagreement (LLM consistently above/below for that paper across metrics).  
  - Isolated bright cells highlight individual outliers worth auditing qualitatively.





```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap-static
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "LLM − Human difference by paper × metric (robust, centered scale; green = lower than Human, orange = higher)."

pair = pair_llm_human(merged)
pair["diff"] = pair["LLM"].astype(float) - pair["Human"].astype(float)

# Pivot and (optionally) reorder by mean bias for readability
hm = pair.pivot_table(index="paper", columns="metric", values="diff", aggfunc="mean")
# Optional ordering (uncomment if you prefer ordered views):
# row_order = np.argsort(np.nanmean(hm.values, axis=1))  # papers by avg diff
# col_order = np.argsort(np.nanmean(hm.values, axis=0))  # metrics by avg diff
# hm = hm.iloc[row_order, col_order]

hm = hm.sort_index()  # or keep your original sort
Z = hm.values.astype(float)

# --- Robust, zero-centered normalization ---
# Use percentile spans to prevent a single outlier from flattening the gradient.
pos = Z[Z > 0]
neg = -Z[Z < 0]
p_hi = np.nanpercentile(pos, 97.5) if pos.size else 0.0
n_hi = np.nanpercentile(neg, 97.5) if neg.size else 0.0
span = max(p_hi, n_hi)
if not np.isfinite(span) or span == 0:
    span = float(np.nanmax(np.abs(Z))) if np.isfinite(np.nanmax(np.abs(Z))) else 1.0

norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-span, vcenter=0.0, vmax=span)

# --- Render ---
fig_hm, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(max(6.5, 0.8*hm.shape[1]), max(6.0, 0.40*hm.shape[0]))
)
im = ax.imshow(
    Z, cmap=UJ_DIV, norm=norm,
    aspect="auto", interpolation="nearest"
)

# Pretty ticks
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(hm.shape[1]), labels=[c.replace("_", " ").title() for c in hm.columns], rotation=40, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(hm.shape[0]), labels=hm.index.tolist())

# Light gridlines between cells
ax.set_xticks(np.arange(-0.5, hm.shape[1], 1), minor=True)
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-0.5, hm.shape[0], 1), minor=True)
ax.grid(which="minor", color="white", linewidth=0.6)
ax.tick_params(which="minor", bottom=False, left=False)

# Colorbar with symmetric ticks
cb = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.02)
cb.set_label("LLM − Human (points)")

tick_vals = np.linspace(-span, span, 5)
cb.set_ticks(tick_vals)
cb.set_ticklabels([f"{t:.1f}" for t in tick_vals])

ax.set_title("Heatmap: LLM − Human differences by paper × metric (robust scaling)")
plt.tight_layout()

```



```{python}
#| label: fig-heatmap-standardized
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Standardized differences (per metric z-scores) so each column has mean 0, sd 1."

pair = pair_llm_human(merged)
pair["diff"] = pair["LLM"].astype(float) - pair["Human"].astype(float)

Zs = hm_std.values.astype(float)

# Use symmetric span from robust percentiles of |Z|
p_hi = np.nanpercentile(np.abs(Zs), 97.5)
span = max(1.0, p_hi)  # minimum span
norm = TwoSlopeNorm(vmin=-span, vcenter=0.0, vmax=span)

fig_s, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(max(6.5, 0.8*hm_std.shape[1]), max(6.0, 0.40*hm_std.shape[0]))
)

ax.set_yticks(np.arange(-0.5, hm_std.shape[0], 1), minor=True)
```

## Agreement metrics

@tbl-agreement summarizes agreement: Pearson \(r\) captures linear alignment of levels; Spearman \(ρ\) captures rank agreement (monotonic relationship), robust to scale differences. 
We report the mean and median of (LLM − Human) to summarize both average shift and central tendency of the differences and Cohen’s κ (unweighted & quadratic). Because scores are continuous, we discretize both LLM and Human using shared quantile cutpoints (5 bins) and compute the Unweighted κ (exact category agreement beyond chance) and the Quadratic‑weighted κ that penalizes larger disagreements more than smaller ones.

As another indicator of agreement, we check whether each side's credible interval contain the other's point estimate, @tbl-coverage shows the shares across rating categories.

@tbl-calibration shows "calibration" results based on a simple linear regression; @fig-uncert-vs-error plots the width of human raters CI against the difference in ratings; and @tbl-outliers lists the papers with the largest aabsolute difference between LLM and human raters.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-calibration
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Calibration of LLM to Human by metric (Human ≈ intercept + slope·LLM). Includes pre-/post- MAD."

from scipy.stats import linregress

def calibrate_per_metric(merged_df):
    P = pair_llm_human(merged_df)
    rows = []
    for m, g in P.groupby("metric"):
        x, y = g["LLM"].to_numpy(), g["Human"].to_numpy()
        if len(g) >= 2:
            lr = linregress(x, y)  # slope, intercept, rvalue, pvalue, stderr
            yhat = lr.slope * x + lr.intercept
            mad_pre  = float(np.mean(np.abs(x - y)))
            mad_post = float(np.mean(np.abs(yhat - y)))
            rows.append(dict(
                metric=m,
                n=len(g),
                slope=lr.slope, intercept=lr.intercept,
                r2=lr.rvalue**2,
                MAD_pre=mad_pre, MAD_post=mad_post,
                MAD_delta=mad_pre - mad_post
            ))
        else:
            rows.append(dict(metric=m, n=len(g),
                             slope=np.nan, intercept=np.nan, r2=np.nan,
                             MAD_pre=np.nan, MAD_post=np.nan, MAD_delta=np.nan))
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("metric").reset_index(drop=True)
    return out

calib = calibrate_per_metric(merged).copy()
calib_rounded = calib.copy()
for c in ["slope","intercept","r2","MAD_pre","MAD_post","MAD_delta"]:
    calib_rounded[c] = calib_rounded[c].round(3)
calib_rounded
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "CI coverage: does one interval contain the other’s point estimate?"

cov = (merged.dropna(subset=["lower_llm","upper_llm","lower_human","upper_human",
                             "midpoint_llm","midpoint_human"])
              .copy())

cov["human_in_llm"] = (cov["midpoint_human"] >= cov["lower_llm"]) & (cov["midpoint_human"] <= cov["upper_llm"])
cov["llm_in_human"] = (cov["midpoint_llm"]   >= cov["lower_human"]) & (cov["midpoint_llm"]   <= cov["upper_human"])
cov["both_cover"]   = cov["human_in_llm"] & cov["llm_in_human"]

coverage_tbl = (cov.groupby("metric", as_index=False)
                  .agg(N=("paper","size"),
                       human_in_llm=("human_in_llm","mean"),
                       llm_in_human=("llm_in_human","mean"),
                       both_cover=("both_cover","mean")))
coverage_tbl[["human_in_llm","llm_in_human","both_cover"]] = \
    coverage_tbl[["human_in_llm","llm_in_human","both_cover"]].round(2)

# Overall coverage (glue)
overall_cov = dict(
    N=int(len(cov)),
    human_in_llm=float(cov["human_in_llm"].mean()),
    llm_in_human=float(cov["llm_in_human"].mean()),
    both=float(cov["both_cover"].mean())
)
glue("cov_both", overall_cov["both"])
glue("cov_hinl", overall_cov["human_in_llm"])
glue("cov_linh", overall_cov["llm_in_human"])

coverage_tbl
```
